name: Vonage
verdict: No OAuth: each customer admin pastes their Vonage API key and secret, or an Application ID plus private key, with no review in 1-3 days. Sender or number registration may add time (unverified).
needGuide: No — just collect the API key and secret, or the Application ID and private key.

auth.detail: Two mechanisms: API key + secret (Authorization: Basic base64(key:secret); two secrets can be active for rotation) and per-application JWTs signed RS256 with an Application ID and private key (default expiry 15 minutes, max 24 hours). A separate signature secret signs webhooks. No OAuth documented.

effort.timeToProduction: 1-3 days for the connection; sender registration may add time (unverified)

approval.gate: None for credentials. Likely: paid account for production, and number/sender registration (e.g. 10DLC, WhatsApp via Messages API) where applicable; not verified.

scopes.why: No OAuth scopes; applications are limited by their enabled capabilities.
scopes.summary: No OAuth scopes. JWT claims can carry ACL paths to limit access (shown for Client SDK user tokens); applications are limited by enabled capabilities.

cost: Free sign-up; usage-based billing (trial credit likely)
prerequisites: Account and owner: Vonage account owner or admin on a company-owned account creates applications and holds the API secret.
Where you register: Vonage API Dashboard → Applications → Create a new application (enable Voice/Messages/RTC, set webhook URLs, generate keys) and Settings for API key/secret
Cost: Free sign-up; usage-based billing (trial credit likely)

registerAt.path: Vonage API Dashboard → Applications → Create a new application (enable Voice/Messages/RTC, set webhook URLs, generate keys) and Settings for API key/secret

steps.do: Decide per customer: collect API key/secret or an Application ID + private key
Customer creates an application in the Vonage Dashboard and enables the needed capabilities
Build a connect form for key/secret or Application ID + private key; encrypt at rest
Mint RS256 JWTs (15-minute default) in your backend for JWT-based APIs
Validate with a test API call and set the webhook URLs on the customer's application
Verify webhook signatures with the signature secret; support secret rotation

roles.team: Vonage account owner or admin on a company-owned account creates applications and holds the API secret.
roles.console: none documented in the pages read (Dashboard user management likely exists).
roles.customer: Customer admin supplies their API key + secret, or creates an application and shares Application ID plus private key; no customer-side approval flow exists.

testing: Use a trial or test account with your own numbers; JWT apps can be tested with the Vonage CLI.
Trial restrictions (e.g. verified destination numbers) are likely but not confirmed here.

blockers.fix: Prefer a dedicated application with its own private key where the API supports JWT.

blockers.problem: Different Vonage APIs use different auth types
blockers.fix: Check each API's auth before building one flow.

blockers.problem: Private key is shown once at creation
No documented partner or subaccount delegation in the pages read
blockers.fix: Confirm with Vonage if you manage accounts for customers.

automation.agentCan: Write credential capture, JWT minting, webhook verification, test calls and customer-facing setup guides.
automation.humanMust: Customer creates the application or keys; account and billing setup; any number or sender registration.

uncertain: Whether Vonage has partner subaccount or OAuth options for ISVs (not covered in the pages read); trial limits; Dashboard role model.
